problem.title: Trace Transaction Approval Chain with Path
problem.prompt: A fintech platform records every transaction approval request and any subsequent review that was triggered. Each review can spawn a new review by a different team or analyst, forming an approval chain. Write a recursive CTE query that returns all transactions and their complete approval paths from the initial request through to the final decision. For each transaction, return the transaction_id, the full path of reviewer_ids visited (as a comma-separated string in traversal order), the depth of the approval chain, and the final status. Start from rows where parent_review_id IS NULL (initial submissions). A transaction may have multiple independent chains if it was submitted multiple times; include all chains. Order results by transaction_id ascending, then depth descending.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE transaction_reviews (review_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, transaction_id INTEGER NOT NULL, parent_review_id INTEGER, reviewer_id INTEGER NOT NULL, review_status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, reviewed_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL); CREATE INDEX idx_parent ON transaction_reviews(parent_review_id);
hints: Consider which rows represent the start of an approval chain and use them as your anchor case.
In the recursive step, join the CTE to itself via parent_review_id to traverse child reviews, concatenating reviewer_ids and incrementing depth.
To get the final status for each chain, you'll need to identify the leaf nodes (reviews with no children) after the recursion completes.
problem.answer_key: WITH RECURSIVE approval_chain AS (SELECT review_id, transaction_id, reviewer_id, review_status, CAST(reviewer_id AS TEXT) AS approval_path, 1 AS chain_depth FROM transaction_reviews WHERE parent_review_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.review_id, c.transaction_id, c.reviewer_id, c.review_status, p.approval_path || ',' || c.reviewer_id, p.chain_depth + 1 FROM transaction_reviews c INNER JOIN approval_chain p ON c.parent_review_id = p.review_id), leaf_nodes AS (SELECT ac.transaction_id, ac.approval_path, ac.chain_depth, ac.review_status AS final_status FROM approval_chain ac WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transaction_reviews tr WHERE tr.parent_review_id = ac.review_id)) SELECT transaction_id, approval_path, chain_depth, final_status FROM leaf_nodes ORDER BY transaction_id ASC, chain_depth DESC;

_meta.scenario: a fintech app tracking transaction approvals and fraud flags

user_solution:
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
    -- Anchor: starting reviews (parent_review_id IS NULL)
    SELECT
        review_id,
        transaction_id,
        reviewer_id::text AS approval_path,
        1 AS chain_depth,
        review_status AS final_status
    FROM transaction_reviews
    WHERE parent_review_id IS NULL

    UNION ALL

    -- Recursive step: extend the chain with each child review
    SELECT
        t.review_id,
        t.transaction_id,
        c.approval_path || ',' || t.reviewer_id,
        c.chain_depth + 1,
        t.review_status
    FROM transaction_reviews t
    JOIN chain c ON t.parent_review_id = c.review_id
)
-- Keep only leaf rows (no further children)
SELECT
    c.transaction_id,
    c.approval_path,
    c.chain_depth,
    c.final_status
FROM chain c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM transaction_reviews t
    WHERE t.parent_review_id = c.review_id
)
ORDER BY c.transaction_id ASC, c.chain_depth DESC;
